SO_2
 (there are no Class II standards for NOx).
Three types of meteorological conditions may produce short-term (3 to 24-hour) high values of ground level concentrations resulting from the stack released emissions. Description of these conditions which include are given mixing (trapping), inversion breakup, and fanning with impaction are given in Appendix J. All of these conditions result in one form or another from atmospheric inversions. Based upon the models and assumptions presented in Appendix J maximum short-term concentrations were computed and compared to the appropriate air quality standards.
The maximum 3-hour sulfur dioxide concentration during limited mixing was calculated at about 160 ug/m<sup>3</sup> and occurred at approximately 10 kilometers downwind. This is well below the short-term sulfur dioxide standards and is 22 percent of the allowable Class II increment.
